Contract.title: One lifecycle adapter over harness task facilities, with bounded role handoffs
Contract.Problem: Control-center interventions I-007 and I-011, approved 2026-11-16, record P-014 and P-018: the OMP case duplicated orchestration instructions, assigned verification and scheduling to conflicting owners, required ledger repairs, treated preparation as a separate conversation, and made workers rediscover installation roots. The framework must keep one GRACE lifecycle while using the harness's native task mechanics.
Contract.Change: `grace5-orchestrate` becomes a thin lifecycle adapter: harness task facilities own spawning, messaging, waiting, cancelling, inspection and transient progress; the adapter owns change selection, isolation decisions and the next lifecycle phase, reading `grace5 status` and the existing lifecycle skills. One implementer is active in a shared worktree; implementers run baseline, targeted and final evidence; the orchestrating agent validates status and the complete diff rather than repeating fresh evidence on an unchanged candidate. A material revision is prepared in the same conversation as its trigger, produces the contract and independent brief, and presents only the unresolved owner decision; execution resumes only under an approval of that revision, and an approval of the exact unchanged revision is reused. The run keeps one compact prose checkpoint under `.grace5/orchestration/runs/` recording the workspace, selected and excluded changes, original starts, worker identity and deadline where not otherwise recoverable, fix-round count, parked obligations and unsettled decisions. Dispatch packets carry verified repository and documentation roots, shell convention, change id, original start and current candidate, permitted role and return stage; `grace5 --help` prints the installed documentation root. Reviewer packets contain only the contract, complete diff, receipts and cited rules, never author reasoning.

Constraints.Constraint: The change revises orchestration and preparation guidance only: no command, flag, schema, record kind, receipt field, second task runtime, registry, database or OMP prerequisite is added, and exact-revision authorization, serial shared-worktree isolation, truthful fresh evidence, complete-diff review and kernel closure stay.
Each change keeps its original start and complete start-to-final diff; later batch commits remain visible and Protected paths still apply.
No approval is inferred: preparation and every material revision return to the owner gate, and an existing approval of unchanged bytes is reused rather than re-requested.
L-24 is amended with the reduced adapter and checkpoint cost, the P-014 failure, the smallest alternative and a removal criterion; no other mechanism is added.
Canonical skills, method text, help text and generated packages change; an ordinary change does not bump the version, pin, tag, README status line or a migration row.

A higher-priority harness policy that conflicts with the adapter is reported before dispatch; skill prose never claims to override it. A capability fallback uses equivalent native task tools and discloses unavailable independence.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No OMP configuration, session-file or path prerequisite; a non-OMP harness keeps the same invariants with its native task tools.
No second GRACE task runtime, tool registry, persistent task database or duplicate progress ledger.
No change to execute or review mechanics beyond cited pointers; their check, receipt, approval and closure semantics stay.
No dependency-policy redesign, advisor scheduling, commit-trailer automation, installation-mirror repair or M3 measurement.
No kernel command, schema, receipt format, source-identity rule, migration boundary or release.

Acceptance.Criterion: An approved batch in one shared worktree keeps at most one active implementer, uses no forced fan-out or duplicate task runtime, and requires implementer receipts and independent review before kernel closure.

An owner request for a material revision produces the contract and independent brief in the same conversation and presents only the unresolved owner decision; no product execution occurs under the unapproved revision.
An approval of the exact unchanged revision is reused without a repeated question or a new approval record.
A red baseline and a later green final result are recorded honestly; generic orchestration neither forbids lifecycle-valid partial commits nor repeats a full final run without changed inputs.

An interrupted run with an active worker or parked change reconciles worker, git and status, restores the next obligation, preserves the original start and performs no duplicate start, dispatch or close.
A reviewer receives the approved contract, complete diff, receipts and cited rules, and no authoring conversation or hinted findings.
A conflicting higher-priority harness policy is exposed before dispatch, with no claim that skill prose overrides it and no silent relaxation of a GRACE gate.

The help change compiles; `grace5 --help` and the generated CLI reference name the installed documentation root, so a fresh session can orient from an installed layout without filesystem-wide guesses.

Manual.Procedure: Rehearse, in an OMP session and one non-OMP task path, an approved serial batch and an interrupted worker. Record: at most one active implementer; same-conversation preparation of a requested revision with only the unresolved owner decision asked; reuse of an approval of unchanged bytes; an honest red baseline; a reviewer packet with the contract, complete diff, receipts and cited rules and no authoring conversation; recovery that reconciles worker, git and status without a duplicate start, dispatch or close; and a pre-dispatch critical stop when the harness policy conflicts with the adapter. On each path, locate the lifecycle documents from the printed documentation root and from an installed layout, not by a filesystem-wide guess.

Decisions.Decision: Harness task facilities own spawn, message, wait, cancel, inspection and transient progress; the GRACE adapter owns authority, isolation, phase selection and closure.
Preparation is a lifecycle phase, not a separate conversation: a requested material revision is prepared and briefed in the triggering conversation, and only the real owner decision is asked.
Live execution uses native progress state; the prose checkpoint holds only what is not durably recoverable and is updated on handoff, changed obligation, pause or finish, not on every status read.
Implementers run baseline, targeted and final evidence; the orchestrating agent validates status and the complete diff at handoff and does not repeat fresh evidence on an unchanged candidate.

Dispatch packets are role-bounded and carry verified repository and documentation roots, shell convention, change id, original start and current candidate, permitted role and return stage; reviewer packets carry no author reasoning.

A conflicting higher-priority harness policy is a critical stop before dispatch; the capability fallback uses equivalent native tools and discloses unavailable independence rather than weakening a gate.
No OMP path, session file or configuration is a kernel prerequisite; another harness receives the same invariants through its own task tools.
